tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (slow storage, alarm fired, production-readiness, sizing requests) rather than implementation details, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including metric names and implicit phrasing cases ('even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower'), and ends with an explicit exclusion scope. It is a dense but still cohesive paragraph appropriate for the breadth of the skill.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user wants to know why Amazon EBS storage is slow, why an EBS alarm fired, or whether their EBS setup is production-ready, even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower or ask whether to add IOPS.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general AWS/EBS concepts the agent already knows and goes straight into domain-specific routing, verdict format, and non-obvious rules specific to this skill's workflow. Some sections are dense but all content is project/domain specific rather than generic exposition.
tests.evidence: Use this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account's Amazon EBS setup. It has two modes.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains routing tables and workflow instructions that point to reference files rather than embedding detailed API docs, error tables, or threshold values inline. Gotchas are concise facts, not large data blocks.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown links in the body, either in the classification table, workflow steps, or the References section at the end.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific condition or trigger phrase (e.g., alarm type, user phrasing) rather than a generic 'see for details' mention.
tests.evidence: | "My app is slow", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics... | Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md) |

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference file links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal patterns.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (modification proposals, approval flow, verdict format) are given exact prescriptive steps while review/investigation framing retains some flexibility, matching prescriptiveness to the fragility of each task.
tests.evidence: Every proposed change follows [Change proposals](references/finding-logic.md#change-proposals): exact command, expected effect, modifications left in the 24-hour window, rollback, and the approval statement.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present multiple competing tools/approaches as equal options; routing table designates one path per scenario and workflow steps are singular/sequential.
tests.evidence: The classification table maps each scenario to exactly one path and reference file, with no competing alternatives offered.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classification and verdict procedure applicable to any EBS troubleshooting/review request, not a one-off task declaration.
tests.evidence: Follow the numbered procedure in the loaded path. Discover every value from the APIs... Then draft the report in the format below.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated Gotchas section with specific, non-obvious domain facts that correct likely agent mistakes (e.g., unit conversions, metric dimension requirements).
tests.evidence: `DescribeInstanceTypes` reports EBS bandwidth in MB/s. Convert it to MiB/s before comparing it with volume throughput.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured reports (troubleshoot verdict, review report) and templates for these are provided via referenced format files rather than omitted.
tests.evidence: Review mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The troubleshoot verdict format listed inline is short (6 bullet items, well under 20 lines) and the larger review report format is offloaded to a reference file.
